story.vex: You never even sorted your own secrets. We didn't have to break in. We just walked up. (Commander Vex, Planet Doom)
story.victory: DOOM ATTACK REPELLED. Every secret file now stays with its owner. Astro: "Protect the data itself, not just the door. That is data-centric security."

files.C:\\Citadel\\README.txt:
ORDERS FROM ASTRO
=================
We found files sitting around unsorted, readable by anyone who's logged in — including a captured Doom intern account. Classify each one, then lock the secret ones down.

1. type starmap-copy.txt and crew-roster.txt
2. classify each file: secret or public
3. icacls the secret ones so only the crew (not doom_intern) can read them
files.C:\\Citadel\\starmap-copy.txt: A working copy of the route home. If Doom gets this, they get everything.
files.C:\\Citadel\\crew-roster.txt: Public roster: Astro (Captain), Rivet (Engineer), Volt (Shield Tech), Cadet (Shield Cadet). No addresses, no codes.

steps.title: Volt's Drill: prove the leak
steps.body: Volt: "A captured Doom intern account can still read our files. That's the leak. Prove it, then we fix it." Read both files with `type`, so we know exactly what's exposed.

steps.title: Classify and lock it down
steps.body: Astro: "Data-centric security means the protection travels with the data, not just the door." Classify each file (`classify starmap-copy.txt secret` or `public`), then deny the captured account access to whichever one is secret: `icacls starmap-copy.txt /deny doom_intern:F`.

objectives.label: doom_intern is denied access to the starmap copy
